note: Blue Rain = glossary (blue-striped underwear).

en: Plan: Hug Decoykins
note: Decoykins = glossary pet name (Milonya's) for Decoy. 'Operation Hug Decoykins' (23) exceeds 22.

en: Don't Call Me Cute!
Formless Treasure
note: Matches the old man's line 'Knowledge is a treasure without form' (wmap slice_15 rows 1171/1179).

en: The Emera Program
An Outcast's Path
note: Lit. 'the way a person in the shadows lives'.

en: Martial Arts Tourney
note: 'Martial Arts Tournament' (23) exceeds 22; the corpus uses 'Martial Arts Tournament' only in a designer label (chap slice_021 row 1726).

en: Magical Party
note: As in chap slice_013 row 1083.

en: What Makes a King
note: Lit. 'one who is a king' (Fairy King Meem's quest).

en: LooKing foR SomeOne...
note: Source mixes stray katakana into hiragana to show the woman's broken speech (desc: 'a woman of broken speech'); mimicked with odd capitals. Exactly 22 bytes.

en: Strange Box Garden
note: Item name as in chap slice_012 rows 939/1005; 18/18 bytes.

en: Dice of Fate Jackpot
note: Dice of Fate = glossary (ITEM.CSV:467). boromouke = rake in a fortune.

en: Geezers' Wand
note: Glossary item name (ITEM.CSV:158).

en: A Clouded Heart
The Aging Songstress
note: Songstress as for Arlotte (wmap slices 17-18).

en: Yo! Bunch of Softies!
note: Glossary: ohitoyoshi-domo = 'softies' (Zonette's word for the party).

en: Love's Smuggling Run
note: bin = delivery/shipment; Barjeff's 'confidential parcel' for the Empress.

en: Casino
Secret Service
note: Special service at the Love Jacuzzi.

en: Put Something On!!
note: haku = put on (lower garments); the quest is about Nora not wearing panties.

en: Tarrit's Close Call!
Mandelgius's Trial 1
Mandelgius's Trial 2
Mandelgius's Trial 3
Mandelgius's Trial 4
Can't Get Out~
note: Echoes Tarrit's line 'I can't get out~' (chap slice_002 row 145); she is stuck in a crack.

en: Crumbling Stone Tablet
note: As in chap slice_003 row 207 'crumbling stone tablet'; 22/22 bytes.

en: Old School Ghost Story
note: kyuu-kousha = old school building; kitan = strange tale. 22/22 bytes.

en: Don't Pick on Me
note: As in the Garden Keeper's line 'D-don't pick on me' (chap slice_010 row 841).

en: Ogre Bay Cleanup Op.
note: Ogre Bay = glossary. sakusen = operation.

en: The Ruler's Amusement
note: ryoushu = lord of a domain; identity unknown (the Molder hint itself asks who it is), so gender-neutral 'Ruler' rather than 'Lord'. yokyou = entertainment/diversion.

en:
When you meet King Balgert, he tells you to
find the Light Ruins, and hands you a
compass.
And so you set out for the Konnu Plains Ruins.
note: hikari no ikou = 'Light Ruins', matching the event title in slice_02 row 181 ('Find the Light Ruins'); not the glossary Lightstair Ruins (hikari no kaiseki).

en:
Following King Balgert's suggestion,
you head for the Temple of Rafa.

You have found the Lightstair Ruins, but its
light is already gone. To restore it, you
must place the Three Phantom Stones
in the three altars.

You have found the Lightstair Ruins, but its
light is already gone. To restore it, you
must place the Three Phantom Stones
in the three altars.
note: Same text as row 243 (source differs only by trailing full-width spaces).

en:
Empress Rianna is building a magic airship to
fly straight into the Palace of the Sun and
take it back from the Kin of Darkness. But
the work is proving very hard, and you are
ordered to get the 'Selcoa Paint' needed to
coat the hull.

To keep the magic airship out of unforeseen
trouble, the movements of the heavens must
be predicted. You are ordered to report
the 'Celestial Readings'.

The last material needed to fly the magic
airship: the 'Wing Soul'. Said to be a
shining wing that gained a soul, it is also
called the wings of all beings. Empress
Rianna has tried everything but has yet to
find it. You are ordered to seek it
your own way.
note: Compressed to fit 260 bytes; all clauses kept.

en:
Ogre Bay, led by King Fulgrant, has a bold
plan: shoot down the Palace of the Sun with
a cannon. But the cannon design drawn by
the King's father, 'The Old Man's
Blueprints', has been lost. You are to find
it using the compass.

You found 'Old Man's Plans', but it
turns out the 'Cannon Tools' needed to build
the cannon were lost too.
Once again, you must search, this time for
the 'Cannon Tools'.

With 'Old Man's Plans' and the
'Cannon Tools' in hand, only the building is
left. But King Fulgrant declares that the
cannon's debut must be a big festival, with
'Seasoned Snacks' to nibble on. And so
you must search yet again.
note: No pronoun for Fulgrant (glossary gender unknown).

en:
Perpeco Village in the Perpeco Forest is under
attack by monsters. You can't just leave it.
Hurry, adventurers!

A chatty sapling with plenty of demands about
where it will put down roots. Where could
there be a place that satisfies it?
note: chatty sapling lowercase in running text, per glossary.

en:
The sapling says it needs some wonderful
fertilizer in order to grow.
Where could you possibly get some,
and how?

Lumisthenes has been attacked by someone.
Join forces with everyone and defend
the city!

The far, far distant tale of certain fairies,
held within the Sun Prison Shrine.
And the one who tells it is...
note: Youryou no zushi is not in the glossary; corpus has 'Sun Prison Shrine' (chap slice_016 rows 1266-1267, key-item line) and 'Sun Cage Reliquary' (chap slice_019 row 1534). Used the key-item form, as slice_02 row 196 does; needs a glossary decision.

en:
Humans, elves, ogres, and... Bearing all of
their hopes, the adventurers have at last
reached the Palace of the Sun.
Can you save the land?

You have retaken the Palace of the Sun and
spared the land from collapse. Evil beings,
monsters, the scars of past tragedy: these
will never vanish, but your deeds were
beyond doubt. Praise the great
adventurers!

King Balgert still seems concerned about the
Palace of the Sun. Once again you head for
the stage of the final battle,
the Palace of the Sun.
And there...

You passed through the door the librarian
led you to. Beyond it spread a land you had
never seen.
note: librarian lowercase per glossary.

en:
The Palace of the Sun, thought to be the
beginning and the end of everything.
But its role was not yet over. Yes, there
are still those who cannot let their
story end...

"You'll cause trouble in the shop!" -- and
so you aren't allowed to form a mixed party
of Good and Evil. Just then, Mucha sets
you a challenge.
note: Opening line is Mucha's reason, set off in quotes. Good/Evil capitalised as glossary alignment terms; 'mixed party' as in wmap slice_06 row 445.

en:
Old Zeppo the dragonewt asks you to gather
a Crystal Flower "for my late wife."
note: Source quotes the old man's words; kept as a quote.

en:
Since Gia is injured, you are more or less
forced to go with Toner to a health checkup
in her place.
note: 'her' = Gia (female per glossary); no pronoun for Toner (gender unknown).

en:
Word is that Hardy the Money-Grubber is
looking after a graveyard.
Why do something that earns no money?
note: Hardy: gender unknown, no pronoun.

en:
King Balgert is pushing Fena to train more
adventurers, but the Training Hall is
understaffed. You are asked to find someone
ideal for training the rookies. There seems
to be more on Fena's mind.
note: Fena: gender unknown, name repeated instead of a pronoun (slice_02 row 206 note says 'her', unsupported by the glossary).

en:
He claims that prosperity shows most in
amusements and luxuries. Right or not, he
seems, in his own way, to be worried about
the state of the town.
note: Source says kare (he): the cookie-eating noble of wmap slice_10 row 768.

en:
Madulay, the artisan who builds the magic
airship, asks you to go and get whetstones
for the job.
note: Madulay: gender unknown; 'artisan' for shokunin, no pronoun.

en:
Every night Shimerief sits in the watchtower
and will not budge. Asked why, she dodges
the question, but...

Toner is looking for Blue Rain. Blue Rain
seems to be very important to Toner.
Blue Rain is apparently 'something exciting.'
Blue Rain, Blue Rain,
exciting Blue Rain...
note: wakuwaku = 'exciting' per glossary. Toner: no pronoun.

en:
Out of her obsessive devotion to Decoy,
she hits on the idea of setting a trap.
All for love's sake...
note: she = Milonya (female; Decoykins quest). Source says kanojo.

en:
He surely never wished to look
the way he does.
That is why he hatches a plan.
note: Source says kare (he); who it is (the 'Don't Call Me Cute!' quest) is not named here.

en:
Knowledge, however much you store, takes up
no space and can be carried anywhere. Today
too, the old man goes on passing it on.

Counselor Emera's healing program.
All who carry darkness in their hearts,
come along now.
note: kaunseraa = Counselor (Emera's glossary position is 'Soul Therapist').

en:
They should have shared the same lot, so why
did they turn out so different?
A thief and a girl. What was it that set
the two apart?
Once the thief learns it, what will go
through the thief's mind?
note: Thief: gender unknown, noun repeated instead of a pronoun.

en:
In the Martial Arts Wing of Santorea Academy,
you can fight Professor Rombino!
Win it all, and something good
might happen.
note: Professor Rombino as in chap slice_013. butsujutsu-tou = Martial Arts Wing (building of the Academy).

en:
In the Magic Wing of Santorea Academy,
you can fight Professor Nambino!
Win it all, and something good
might happen.
note: Professor Nambino as in chap slice_013.

en:
Ghosts have appeared, troubling the fairy
village. On the orders of Meem, the Fairy
King, you were tasked with driving them out.
note: Meem, the Fairy King as in chap slice_018 row 1464.

en:
A woman of broken speech and a foul-mouthed
man. The pair ask you to help find someone.

A strange box garden: set it up in 'a certain
place' and it activates, drawing you into the
little garden for all kinds of exploring.
Now, where might 'a certain place' be?

What is gambling? A heap of numbers, or
something decided by fate?
That eternal question is about to be settled
by the fortune-teller Natori.

The Central Council, where many views are
gathered and debated. Its Council Chair is
Wattner.
Lately he seems rather worn out.
note: Source uses kare (he) for Wattner here; glossary has gender unknown -- evidence for a glossary update.

en:
Driven by ambition and a thirst for knowledge,
she carries on her research. And her dislike
of adventurers had its reasons.
note: Source says kanojo (she); the researcher at the Stargazing Lighthouse, not named here.

en:
'Let song speak, let verse sing.' A singer
should speak through song, yet from her lips
come only words of longing for the old days.
What is on the aging songstress's mind?
note: Opening is a set phrase (uta wa katare yo, shi wa utae); rendered as a quoted maxim. her = the songstress (Arlotte, female).

en:
She has values of her own. That blatant lie
may have some purpose behind it.
note: Zonette's quest (ctx). Source says kanojo (she), and the hint also says kanojo -- evidence for Zonette's glossary gender (currently unknown). Dropped the source's trailing line break.

en:
A man living out 'love saves the world'
to the letter. He plotted to smuggle love.
note: Barjeff's quest (ctx 'Chief Barjeff'); source says otoko/kare (man/he).

en:
Good day to you,
and welcome to MILL.GP.
Honored guest, might I interest you in a
game with me today?
note: MILL.GP. per glossary; greeting style as the dealer Linesman in wmap slice_18 row 1401.

en:
The Love Jacuzzi has a special service of its
own for valued customers.
But for that, something is needed.
note: Rabu Jakujii romanized 'Love Jacuzzi' (new name). Source o-toku-sama is a typo for o-tokui-sama (valued customers).

en:
Do different races have different senses of
shame? Nora doesn't mind at all, but
her coworker Yuna fusses over Nora's
underwear.
note: Yuna: gender unknown, no pronoun. 'her' = Nora.

en:
Her ordeals never end.
Or is it you, the ones involved with her,
upon whom the ordeals are truly falling...?
note: her = Tarrit (female).
